problem_text:
A distribution center must devise a procurement and storage strategy for a critical perishable ingredient over a forecast window of 17 consecutive weeks.  
The starting stockpile at the onset of the planning interval is 64 kilograms.  
In each week \( t = 1, \dots, 17 \), the vendor permits the center to submit a procurement request whose amount must be between 1 and 66 kilograms.  
Nevertheless, every request submitted will incur a lead time of 4 weeks before the ingredient becomes available to fulfill requirements or augment the stockpile.  
The weekly requirement for the ingredient is specified as follows:  
* Week 1: requirement 17 kilograms  
* Week 2: requirement 40 kilograms  
* Week 3: requirement 55 kilograms  
* Week 4: requirement 38 kilograms  
* Week 5: requirement 42 kilograms  
* Week 6: requirement 56 kilograms  
* Week 7: requirement 20 kilograms  
* Week 8: requirement 44 kilograms  
* Week 9: requirement 16 kilograms  
* Week 10: requirement 18 kilograms  
* Week 11: requirement 33 kilograms  
* Week 12: requirement 56 kilograms  
* Week 13: requirement 37 kilograms  
* Week 14: requirement 42 kilograms  
* Week 15: requirement 18 kilograms  
* Week 16: requirement 15 kilograms  
* Week 17: requirement 50 kilograms  

Stockouts are tolerated, but any unsatisfied requirement is considered lost and will not be deferred to a later date.  
Throughout the planning window, ingredient amounts may be treated as continuous quantities, and the total quantity of physical stock held at any moment must not surpass the cold-storage capacity of 64 kilograms.  

In week 17, the maximum allowable procurement amount is restricted to 42 kilograms.  
In week 13, the physical stock on hand must be no less than 39 kilograms.  

The aggregate expense over the planning horizon comprises three elements: the procurement expense, which amounts to 2 per kilogram ordered; the storage expense, which amounts to 1 per kilogram of stock transferred from one week to the next; and the shortage penalty, which amounts to 12 per kilogram of unmet requirement. Determine the optimal procurement quantity for each week and monitor the consequent stockpile and shortage volumes so as to minimize the total expense.
